name: Chicken Parmesan
description: Kenji's gold-standard chicken parm: buttermilk-marinated cutlets with a shatteringly crisp breadcrumb crust, quick San Marzano sauce, and bubbly mozzarella. A Sunday comfort classic that Elsie will devour.
why: Kenji's buttermilk marinade keeps the chicken impossibly juicy under that crispy crust — the definitive version.

name: Grilled Chicken with Lemon and Herbs
description: Simple bone-in chicken pieces marinated in lemon, olive oil, garlic, and fresh herbs, grilled over a two-zone fire until charred and juicy. Perfect for a 75°F Monday evening on the grill.
why: Food52's guide nails the two-zone technique for juicy, charred results — thighs are forgiving and kid-friendly.

name: Babo Pasta (Homemade Spinach Egg Yolk Pasta)
description: The family's beloved Babo Pasta: silky homemade spinach pasta made with 00 flour, blanched spinach purée, and rich egg yolks only — no whole eggs. Roll thin, cut into tagliatelle, and toss with brown butter and parmesan or a simple garlic-olive oil sauce.
why: Food52's Meryl Feinstein recipe provides the closest framework to the family's egg-yolk-only technique with proper spinach-to-flour ratios.

name: Corned Beef Hash with Yellow Potatoes
description: Crispy, golden corned beef hash made with Yukon Gold potatoes for a creamy, buttery interior. Par-boil diced potatoes, then pan-fry in cast iron with shredded corned beef and onions until deeply crusty. Crown with fried eggs.
why: Serious Eats' method of par-boiling then pressing in cast iron creates the crispiest crust with creamy potato centers.

name: Grilled Steaks with Potatoes, Peppers, and Cilantro Chimichurri
description: Thick-cut ribeye or NY strip steaks grilled over high heat, served alongside grilled bell peppers and roasted baby potatoes, all drizzled with a vibrant cilantro-parsley chimichurri sauce with red wine vinegar punch.
why: Splendid Table's recipe nails the steak-chimichurri-potato trinity with a restaurant-quality approach to grilled potatoes.

name: Homemade Pizza Night (No Pork)
description: Kenji's no-knead overnight pizza dough baked on a screaming-hot steel or stone. For guests Sophia and Faran: set up a topping bar with fresh mozzarella, roasted red peppers, artichoke hearts, olives, basil, cherry tomatoes, and ricotta — absolutely no pork products.
why: Kenji's pan pizza is foolproof, crispy-bottomed, and endlessly customizable — perfect for a crowd with dietary restrictions.

name: Grilled Smash Burgers with Green Goddess Salad
description: Thick, juicy smash-style burgers from 80/20 chuck on a hot grill, served on toasted brioche buns with all the fixings. Paired with a vibrant green goddess salad as the meal's signature side — the craving fulfilled.
why: Serious Eats' burger method delivers maximum crust and juiciness — the perfect canvas for Saturday's green goddess pairing.

name: Whipped Ricotta and Pea Crostini with Mint
description: Toasted baguette rounds topped with lemon-whipped ricotta, bright blanched spring peas, shaved radishes, fresh mint, and a drizzle of good olive oil. Light, seasonal, and gone in seconds.
why: Peas and ricotta are spring's perfect pairing — this disappears fast and works before any of the week's dinners.

name: Grilled Asparagus with Romesco Dip
description: Thick asparagus spears grilled until lightly charred, served with a smoky-sweet romesco sauce made from roasted red peppers, almonds, garlic, and smoked paprika. A stunning spring starter.
why: Peak asparagus season meets the grill — the romesco adds depth without heaviness and pairs well with the week's grilled mains.

name: Spring Composed Salad with Asparagus, Peas, and Goat Cheese
description: A dinner-sized composed salad arranged on a platter: blanched asparagus and sugar snap peas, fresh English peas, shaved radishes, soft goat cheese, toasted pistachios, and fresh herbs over a bed of butter lettuce and arugula.
dressing: Lemon-Herb Vinaigrette: Whisk 1/3 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp honey, 1 minced garlic clove, 2 tbsp chopped fresh dill and mint, salt and pepper to taste.
flavor_rationale: The bright lemon vinaigrette lifts the earthy asparagus and sweet peas, while creamy goat cheese and crunchy pistachios add richness and texture contrast. Fresh herbs tie every component to the spring garden.
seasonal_note: Peak East Coast April: asparagus, English peas, sugar snaps, and radishes are all at their sweetest and crunchiest right now.
why: This composed beauty showcases everything April has to offer — substantial enough for a standalone dinner with crusty bread.

name: Green Goddess Salad
description: A big, vibrant tossed dinner salad with chopped romaine, cucumber, avocado, snap peas, radishes, green onions, and fresh herbs, all coated in a creamy herb-packed Green Goddess dressing. The craving, satisfied.
dressing: Green Goddess Dressing: Blend 1/2 cup Greek yogurt, 1/2 cup packed fresh herbs (parsley, basil, chives, tarragon), 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 small garlic clove, 1 anchovy fillet (optional), salt and pepper until smooth and vibrant green.
flavor_rationale: The creamy, tangy dressing is a celebration of fresh spring herbs — tarragon and basil bring anise sweetness, chives add onion bite, and lemon keeps everything bright. Crunchy vegetables provide contrast to the lush dressing.
seasonal_note: Spring herbs are at their most fragrant in mid-April — tarragon, chives, and basil from the garden or farmers market make this dressing sing.
why: The week's craving fulfilled — paired with Saturday's burgers, this is the dinner salad that makes the whole meal feel like an event.

name: Strawberry, Radish, and Arugula Salad with Poppy Seed Vinaigrette
description: A quick, colorful side salad of peppery arugula tossed with sliced strawberries, thin-shaved radishes, crumbled feta, and toasted almonds in a sweet-tart poppy seed vinaigrette.
dressing: Poppy Seed Vinaigrette: Whisk 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp poppy seeds, pinch of salt and pepper.
flavor_rationale: Sweet strawberries and peppery radishes are a classic spring contrast — the poppy seed vinaigrette bridges their flavors while arugula adds a pleasant bite.
seasonal_note: Virginia strawberries begin their season in mid-April and radishes are abundant at every farmers market — this salad is the taste of the moment.
why: A bright, beautiful side that pairs especially well with the grilled meats (Monday, Thursday, Saturday) without competing.

name: Shaved Asparagus and Parmesan Salad with Lemon
description: Raw asparagus shaved into ribbons with a vegetable peeler, tossed with shaved parmesan, toasted pine nuts, a squeeze of lemon, and peppery olive oil. Elegant, crunchy, and ready in 5 minutes.
dressing: Simple Lemon Dressing: Whisk 3 tbsp best-quality olive oil, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, flaky sea salt, and freshly cracked black pepper. Toss just before serving.
flavor_rationale: Raw asparagus has a grassy sweetness that parmesan's umami richness amplifies — lemon brightens everything and pine nuts add buttery crunch. Minimalist and perfect.
seasonal_note: April asparagus is at its thinnest and most tender — ideal for shaving raw, a technique that showcases the season's best spears.
why: An elegant 5-minute side that elevates Tuesday's Babo Pasta or Sunday's Chicken Parm with zero effort.

name: Strawberry Basil Lemonade
description: Fresh-squeezed lemonade muddled with ripe strawberries and torn basil leaves, lightly sweetened with simple syrup. Serve over ice in a big pitcher for the family.
why: Strawberries and basil scream April in Virginia — a crowd-pleaser for all ages, especially with Friday's pizza night guests.

name: Cucumber-Lime Agua Fresca
description: Cool, clean, and hydrating: blend English cucumber with fresh lime juice, a touch of sugar, and cold water, then strain for a crystal-clear refresher. Perfect for hot grill nights.
why: As temps climb toward 88°F Saturday, this is the most cooling drink in the rotation — ideal alongside grilled steaks and burgers.

name: Sparkling Rosemary-Citrus Spritzer
description: A rosemary-infused simple syrup shaken with fresh grapefruit and lemon juice, topped with sparkling water. Herbaceous, sophisticated, and family-friendly.
why: The herbal rosemary note pairs beautifully with the week's Italian and Mediterranean flavors — a grown-up feel without the alcohol.
